sentences.text:
As per prosecution case, husband of the first informant, who used to work outside the country,
forced his wife (the first informant) to enter into illicit physical relations with other persons so that they can earn money.

It is alleged in the F.I.R. that when the first informant opposed such activities,
she was threatened with divorce.
It is further alleged in the F.I.R. that in 2021 he returned from Saudi Arabia and brought with him a woman, namely, Fatima, and had sexual relation with her in front of her eyes.
The matter was settled between the two by intervention of relatives.
Thereafter, he returned to Saudi Arabia.

It is alleged in the F.I.R. that as per planning with her husband, she began establishing physical relations with other persons and kept recording the audio so that they could blackmail them and extort money.

Meanwhile, a month before the filing of the application,
applicant- Mohd. Haidar Naqvi (neighbour of the first informant) hacked her mobile and threatened her to make viral all the audio recordings and along with applicant- Hussain Abbas (Devar of the first informant) committed rape on her.

When she protested, the applicants, namely, Hussain Abbas and Mohd. Haidar, threatened her of uploading the audio on social media to make it viral and applicant- Mohd. Haidar sent all the audio recordings on her husband's mobile.
4. It is contended on behalf of the applicants that the F.I.R. is nothing but a bundle of lies.
The story is too improbable to be believed.

The real fact is that the first informant developed illicit relation with one Hasan Akhtar, the real uncle of the co-accused and when this fact came into knowledge of the family members, they tried to stop her from having such adulterous relationship.
The real brother of the instant applicant sent a complaint (paper No. 58) to the police authorities along with a clip, messages and other material for the purpose of taking action against her.

Just after sending this application to the concerned authorities, the first informant, to create a false defence, moved an application u/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. imputing false and frivolous allegations against the applicants, her husband and other members of the family.
The applicants are having no criminal antecedents and are absolutely innocent.

5. Learned counsel for the first informant and learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail pressing before me the fact that the first informant was forced for entering into illicit relations with other persons and the defence story is false.
The allegations as against the present applicants are serious in nature.

They have also been charge-sheeted, therefore, the applicants do not deserve a protection u/s 438 Cr.P.C.
6.

In case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent of accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate entire available material against the accused carefully and that the exact role of the accused has also to be taken into consideration.

entities.text: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. In the instant case, I considered submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicants and all attending facts and circumstances.
In my view, a case for anticipatory bail is made out.
Hence, the present anticipatory bail application is allowed.
